khyber-pakhtunkhwa.name: Nathia Gali
khyber-pakhtunkhwa.description: Ideal for hiking, trekking and sightseeing, with its crowning jewel, Mushkpuri peak, Nathia Gali is the place to experience nature's true beauty.

khyber-pakhtunkhwa.name: Seri Bahlol
khyber-pakhtunkhwa.description: Seri Bahlol, likewise Sahr-I Bahlol or Sahri Bahlol, is a city and archeological site situated close to Takht-I-Bahi, in Mardan District, around 70-kilometer north-west of Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

khyber-pakhtunkhwa.name: Shogran Valley
khyber-pakhtunkhwa.description: Shogran, one of the most beautiful plateaus in Naran Valley.  From the rolling grassy lawns of the rest house, one can see breathtaking panoramic views of snow covered mountains.

khyber-pakhtunkhwa.name: Madyan
khyber-pakhtunkhwa.description: Madyan presents dense, lush greenery under a clear, blue sky. With the rivers and streams that accent the scenery on occasion making one feel closer to nature.

khyber-pakhtunkhwa.name: Sethi street
khyber-pakhtunkhwa.description: Made in the nineteenth century Finely assembled 05 places of Sethi family are situated here close by other houses.

azad-jamu-khashmir.name: Sharada Peeth
azad-jamu-khashmir.description: Sharada Peeth is a ruined Hindu temple and ancient centre of learning between 6th and 12th century CE. It played a key role in the development and popularisation of the Sharada script in North India, causing the script to be named after it.

azad-jamu-khashmir.name: Leepa Valley
azad-jamu-khashmir.description: Leepa Valley is located in Hattian Bala District of Azad Kashmir. With fields of rice apple found all over the valley, its lush green river fields in summer and typical wooden kashmiri houses present a wonderful view to the tourists.

azad-jamu-khashmir.name: Neelum Valley
azad-jamu-khashmir.description: The valley is situated in the northeast of Muzaffarabad, running parallel to Kaghan Valley. It is replete with gorgeous scenery, stunning valleys, and magical waterfalls.

punjab.name: Rohtas Fort
punjab.description: Pashtun King Sher Shah Suri, the founder of short-lived Suri dynasty, built the Rohtas Fort in the 16th century. It is located near the city of Jhelum.

punjab.name: Tomb of Jahangir
punjab.description: The mausoleum dates from 1637, and is located in Shahdara Bagh in Lahore. The site is famous for its interiors that are extensively embellished with frescoes and marble. The tomb is a part of an ensemble currently on the tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage status.

punjab.name: Wagha Border
punjab.description: A village, famous for the Wagah Border ceremony,also serving as a goods transit terminal and a railway station between Pakistan and India. The ceremony happens at the border gate each day. The flag ceremony is conducted by the Pakistan Rangers and Indian Border Security Force.

punjab.name: Nankana Sahib
punjab.description: A small town in Punjab thatâs one of the most sacred locations for Sikhs. The town boasts a beautiful gurdwara with marvelous architecture, which has the power to inspire and amaze.

punjab.name: Harappa
punjab.description: Harappa is a large village, presently in the province of Punjab. The modern town is a part of and lies next to the ancient city. The site of the ancient city contains the ruins of a Bronze Age fortified city.

punjab.name: Harappa
punjab.description: Harappa is a large village, presently in the province of Punjab. The modern town is a part of and lies next to the ancient city. The site of the ancient city contains the ruins of a Bronze Age fortified city.

punjab.name: Khewra Salt Mine
punjab.description: The Khewra Salt Mine is in Khewra, Punjab. Famous for itâs production of pink Khewra salt, often marketed as Himalayan salt, and is a major tourist attraction, drawing thousands of visitors a year.

punjab.name: Gumti Water Fountain
punjab.description: Gumti Water Fountain is a monument in Faisalabad, Pakistan preserved from the British Raj era. It was a general meeting place of the city folk for local town meetings.

punjab.name: Changa Manga Forest
punjab.description: The Changa Manga is a planted forest which includes a wildlife preserve, in the Kasur and Lahore districts of Punjab. The Changa Manga forest was originally planted in 1866 by British foresters. The forest is home to many species of animals.

punjab.name: Fort Munroe Hill
punjab.description: Fort Munro named after a British administrator, Col Munroe is located in Southern Punjab at the foothills of the Suleiman Range. It attracts a number of tourists every year, particularly those who wish to escape from the hot plains of southern Punjab.

punjab.name: Attock Fort
punjab.description: Attock Fort was constructed in 1581 on the orders of the Mughal Emperor Akbar to protect the passage of the River Indus. It is located at a distance of 80 km from the capital city of Islamabad.

punjab.name: Multan Fort
punjab.description: A military installation built between 800 and 1000 B.C. The fort originally known as Katochgarh and is attributed to have been built by the Katoch Dynasty was notable for both its effectiveness as a defense installation and for its architecture.

punjab.name: Wazir Khan Hammam
punjab.description: A Persian-style bath which was built in Lahore in 1635 C.E. during the reign of Emperor Shah Jahan. The Shahi Hammam is the last remaining Mughal-era hammam in Lahore.

punjab.name: Hafeez Jalandhari Tomb
punjab.description: Hafeez Jalandhari was a Pakistani Urdu-language poet who wrote the lyrics for the National Anthem of Pakistan. Buried in Model Town, Lahore later shifted to a tomb built by the Government of Pakistan near Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore, the site of Pakistan Resolution.

punjab.name: Gurdwara Panja Sahib
punjab.description: Gurdwara Panja Sahib Jee is a famous gurdwara located near Islamabad, Hasan Abdal.

punjab.name: Gurdwara Janam Asthan Guru Ram Das Jee
Gurdwara Chakki Sahib Jee
punjab.description: Gurdwara Chakki Sahib Jee, at Eminabad is located where a large millstone chakkis was kept.

punjab.name: Gurdwara Sachi Sauda
punjab.description:
Gudwara sacha sauda is situated in Farooqabad, Sheikhupura Punjab. Guru Nanak as a young man was sent by his father Mehta Kalu to instill a sense of business in 
his son.

punjab.name: Gurdwara Dera Sahib
punjab.description: A Sikh temple in Lahore which commemorates the spot where the 5th guru of Sikhism was martyred in 1606. The gurdwara is located just outside of the Walled City of Lahore and is part of an ensemble of monuments.

punjab.name: Gurdwara Chowa Sahib
punjab.description: Gurdwara Chowa Sahib is an abandoned gurdwara, located at the northern edge of the Rohtas Fort, near Jhelum, Punjab. The current building dates from 1834, and was commissioned by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

punjab.name: Haveli Barood Khana
punjab.description: Built in the 18th century by a Sikh commanding general and used as a house. Considering the hot temperature of Lahore, the haveli has high ceilings. The room also has murals of the Sikh general fighting demons.

punjab.name: Ganda Singh Wala
punjab.description: Ganda Singh Wala is a village in Kasur, Punjab. A daily 6 p.m Beating Retreat Border Ceremony is jointly held at the border crossing by the military of both nations. The ceremony is attended mostly by local Punjabi's on either side of the border.

punjab.name: Tomb of Shah Shams Sabzwari Tabrez
Kasur
punjab.description: Kasur also Romanized as QasÅ«r is a city to south of Lahore, in the Pakistani province of Punjab. It is also known for being the burial place of the 17th-century Sufi-poet Bulleh Shah. Kasur derives its name from the Arabic word qasur meaning âpalaces,â or âfortsâ.

punjab.name: Kallar Kahar
punjab.description: Alluring scenic beauty, with a calm lake, and breathtaking views, where you can go for cliff-diving, paragliding and many more activities.

punjab.name: Soon Valley
punjab.description: Soon Valley is a breathtaking vista of natural beauty consisting of lakes and springs, lush green fertile fields. Accessible through Kallar Kahar, Soon Valley extends to almost 100 kilometers.

punjab.name: Neela Sandh Waterfall
punjab.description: Neela Sandh is a delightful waterfall, situated in Mori Syedan, Rawalpindi, Punjab. It has numerous greenery, tall trees and extensive mountains which are relatively secured with snow constantly. Guests who adore swimming unquestionably visit to enjoy with their families and companions.

punjab.name: Jaulian Buddhist Monastery
punjab.description: Dating from the 2nd century CE, Jaulian monastery along with the nearby monastery at Mohra Muradu, form part of the Ruins of Taxila. Consists of a main central stupa, 27 peripheral smaller stupas, 59 small chapels displaying scenes from the life of Buddha.

punjab.name: Jamia Mosque Bhong
punjab.description: Bhong Mosque is located in the village of Bhong, Rahim Yar Khan District, Punjab Province. It was designed and constructed over a period of nearly 50 years.

punjab.name: Moti Mosque
punjab.description: Moti Masjid is a 17th-century religious building located inside the Lahore Fort, Lahore, and Punjab, Pakistan. It is a small, white marble structure built by Mughal emperor Jahangir.

punjab.name: Swaik Lake
punjab.description: Swaik Lake also known as âKhandowa Lakeâ is located in tehsil Kallar Kahar, Punjab. Itâs crystal clear water and serene atmosphere offers adventure lovers just the right mix of thrill with ease of access. It is a popular tourist attraction and offers opportunities for swimming and diving.

punjab.name: Haveli of Nau Nihal Singh
punjab.description: The haveli is considered to be one of the finest examples of Sikh architecture in Lahore preserved in its original architecture.

punjab.name: Mankiala Stupa
punjab.description: A 2nd-century Buddhist stupa near the village of Tope Mankiala, built to commemorate the spot, where according to the Jataka tales, an incarnation of the Buddha called Prince Sattva sacrificed himself to feed seven hungry tiger cubs.

punjab.name: Taxila Museum
punjab.description: Taxila Museum is situated in Taxila, its collection mainly focuses on Gandharan art dating from the 1st to the 7th centuries CE.  There are some 4000 objects displayed, including stone, stucco, terracotta, silver, gold, iron and semiprecious stones excavated from the ruins of ancient Taxila.

punjab.name: Nigar Khana
punjab.description: Nigar Khana known as a House of Art for selling handicrafts, exhibits antiquities, cultural and artistic items for over 45 years. one finds oneself into a world of colors consisted of mosaic art, Naqashi, wooden, glass work etc.

punjab.name: Qutb-ud-Din Aibak's Tomb
punjab.description: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the Department of Archaeology and Museums which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture. Prior to the modern construction, the Sultan's grave existed in a simple form and was enclosed by residential houses.

punjab.name: Pharwala Fort
punjab.description: Pharwala Fort is a 15th-century fort built by the Gakhars located in Rawalpindi. The fort is naturally defended on one side by a small Himalayan range and the other by the Soan River.

punjab.name: Pindi Food Street
punjab.description: A must visit place for the food lovers, if one is visiting Rawalpindi. There are a variety of restaurants and food to enjoy with family and friends.

punjab.name: Raja Bazaar
punjab.description: Oldest place in Rawalpindi present in the heart of the city. All sorts of things are available for customers at a reasonable price, from retailers to wholesale are present. Crowded by people surfing their time in shopping.

punjab.name: Sadhu da Bagh caves
punjab.description: The village is believed to be more than seven hundred years old. Relics of the Buddhist era, dating back to the 8th century can be found here. Archaeological evidence indicates that the caves and the platform-like formations surrounding the area were first used for meditation.

punjab.name: Shrine Khawaja Awais Kagha
punjab.description: Located in a cemetery in Dera Basti, Multan built around the year 1300 lies the tomb of Khawaja Awais Kagha who was a notable Sufi Wali. The tomb is decorated with blue and white glazed tiles covering the corner towers and portions of the facades.

punjab.name: Shahi Eid Gah Mosque
punjab.description: The mosque was funded by Nawab Abdul Samad Khan, who was the Mughal governor of Multan. The mosque is spacious, with a vast courtyard, a prayer chamber, and features seven domes and the mosque's exterior is embellished with glazed blue Multan-style tiles.

punjab.name: Cholistan
punjab.description: The Cholistan Desert, locally known as Rohi, stretches across southern Punjab, Pakistan, extending into Sindh and the Indian Thar Desert. Covering over 26,000â¯kmÂ², it was once a fertile plain nourished by the ancient Hakra (Ghaggar) River. Today it's home to more than 400 Indus Valley Civilization archaeological sites

punjab.name: Begum Shahi Mosque
punjab.description: A 17th-century mosque situated in the Walled City of Lahore,built between 1611 and 1614 during the reign of Mughal Emperor Jahangir in honor of his mother. One of the earliest surviving example of a Mughal-era mosque.

punjab.name: Delhi Gate
punjab.description: The Delhi Gate was originally built during the Mughal period, served as the main gateway to Lahore, and during the Mughal era its doors were shut every evening. The surrounding area includes several buildings of historical significance near it.

punjab.name: Giri Fort
punjab.description: Giri Fort built in the fifth century perhaps as a stronghold for the thousands of monks in Taxila Valley. Two groups of Buddhist establishments are found here, a fort, a Muslim Ziarat and mosques, all ranging from the early Kushana period to the time of Akbar.

punjab.name: Badshahi Mosque
punjab.description: The Badshahi Mosque of Lahore was constructed by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb between 1671 and 1673 and was the largest mosque in the world from 1673 to 1986.

punjab.name: Sheesh Mahal
punjab.description: The Palace of Mirrors is located within the Shah Burj in Lahore. Constructed under the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1631â1632. It is among the 21 monuments that were built by successive Mughal emperors inside Lahore Fort.

punjab.name: Lahore Fort Food Street
punjab.description: Travelers from all across the world come to feast on some of the most delicious desi food. Offering enchanting views of Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort, the delicious food is bound to make your visit to this food street unforgettable.

punjab.name: Malot Temples
punjab.description: Malot Hindu Temples are located in the Salt Range of Pakistan near the city of Kallar Kahar. A serene place where the cliffs by the temple present a beautiful panoramic view.

punjab.name: The Abbasi Royal Graveyard
punjab.description: The Royal Graveyard of Abbasi family, a large size rectangular room that contains the graves of all the 12 Nawabs that ruled the Bahawalpur State. These tombs display great architectural beauty. Most of them are the typical blue paintwork that is typical of Sind and South Punjab architecture

punjab.name: Noor Mahal
punjab.description: Bahawalpur, due to the lack of publicity.

punjab.name: Shab Bhar Mosque
punjab.description: A colonial era mosque in Lahore, Pakistan. The mosque is said to have been built overnight in 1917 due to a conflict between Hindu and Muslims, regarding ownership of a 3 marla site after a Muslim had offered prayer on the vacant site.

punjab.name: Shab Bhar Mosque
punjab.description: A colonial era mosque in Lahore, Pakistan. The mosque is said to have been built overnight in 1917 due to a conflict between Hindu and Muslims, regarding ownership of a 3 marla site after a Muslim had offered prayer on the vacant site.

punjab.name: Service Club
punjab.description: One of the oldest buildings of Multan, built on Turkish architecture and by making clay bricks from Chenab River constructed in 1880. British officers have used it as a club; they had constructed a big floor of wood in the main hall. It was reconstructed with Mughal theme interior.

punjab.name: Monument of Van Alexander Agnew
punjab.description: This monument was erected by the British East India Company in honor of Patrick Alexander Vans Agnew and Lieutenant W. A. Anderson.

punjab.name: Bhangianwali Toap
punjab.description: The cannon was cast in about 1757 in Lahore, now in Pakistan but at the time part of the Durrani Empire. Displayed in front of the Lahore Museum in Lahore, it was one of the largest cannon ever made in the sub-continent.

punjab.name: Emporium Mall
punjab.description: The most indicatively planned and largest mall in Lahore. This mall is a home to more than 200 brands from local and international chains. Having the largest food court of the city and is dominated with a huge multiplex cinema, banquet halls and supermarket.

punjab.name: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur
punjab.description: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur, also called Kartarpur Sahib, built on the historic site where the founder of Sikhism, Guru Nanak, settled and assembled the Sikh community. Notable for its location near the border between Pakistan and India.

punjab.name: punjab
punjab.description: Punjab, âThe Land of Five Riversâ, is a culturally and historically rich province, with extra-ordinary landscape.

punjab.name: Lahore
punjab.description: A city where history, culture, and hospitality come alive. Explore its grand Mughal monuments, vibrant bazaars, rich cuisine, and lively streets that never sleep.

balochistan.name: Kund Malir Beach
balochistan.description: Kund Malir beach with its sparkling cerulean waters, beckons visitors to spend the day picnicking or the night camping on its peaceful shore. Add a to that bonfire as the Milky Way unfolds above and it makes for the perfect weekend getaway.

balochistan.name: Ziarat Juniper Forest
balochistan.description: The Ziarat Juniper forest is a juniper forest in Ziarat, Balochistan, Pakistan. These forests are spread around the hilly area of Ziarat and Mount Zarghoon

balochistan.name: Hingol National Park,Balochistan
balochistan.description: Hingol National Park is the largest national park in Pakistan and is named after the southern part of the Hangul River which flows along the shores of the Arabian Sea and is home to large numbers of waterfowl and marine life.

balochistan.name: Princess of Hope
balochistan.description: The Princess of Hope is a natural rock formation that manifests a princess looking beyond the horizon. The site is located in the Hingol National Park in the Lasbela District of Balochistan.

balochistan.name: Jiwani Coastal Wetland
balochistan.description: Jiwani is a town and commercial port that is located along the Gulf of Oman in the Gawadar District of the Balochistan province in Pakistan.

balochistan.name: Lahoot Lamakan
balochistan.description: Lahoot Lamakan is a cave in Balochistan, Pakistan. The water flows from the external limestone shell of the cave and believers have a tale that first it was milk when people began to sell it, miraculously it became water.

balochistan.name: Reko Diq Mine
balochistan.description: The Reko Diq Mine is located near Reko Diq town, Balochistan. Reko Diq represents one of the largest copper and gold reserves in the world having estimated reserves of 5.9 billion tonnes of ore.

balochistan.name: Sapat Beach
balochistan.description: Ranked as one of the best beaches in the world, Sapat beach, with its exceptional beauty is the best go-to place with family and friends.

balochistan.name: Wali Tangi Dam Lake
balochistan.description: Wali Tangi Dam is a little dam in the Urak Valley in Balochistan territory of Pakistan. It is arranged around 20 km east of Quetta at a rise of roughly 8,350 ft.

balochistan.name: Quetta
balochistan.description: The city is known as the "Fruit Garden of Pakistan," due to the numerous fruit orchards in and around it, and the large variety of fruits and dried fruit products produced there.

balochistan.name: Urak Valley
balochistan.description: Urak Valley is a valley encircled by mountains inside the Quetta Area of Balochistan Region, in western Pakistan. Urak Valley is found close to Hana Lake and 28 kilometers (17 mi) from Quetta city.

balochistan.name: balochistan
balochistan.description: A land that is yet to be explored by travelers around the world.  Balochistan has managed to preserve its beauty because it has not been urbanised as much as other areas.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Kargah Buddha
gilgit-baltistan.description: About 9.7km away from Gilgit, this carved image is part of an archaeological site which stands 50 feet high.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Attabad Lake
gilgit-baltistan.description: Attabad Lake is in Gojal region of Hunza -a mountainous valley in the northern part of the Gilgit-Baltistan formed by the Hunza River, bordering Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor to the north and the Xinjiang region of China to the northeast.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Rock carvings at Thalpan
gilgit-baltistan.description: Located at the mid-point between Islamabad and Gilgit-Skardu, the rock carvings at Thalpan are in Chilas Valley, Gilgit

gilgit-baltistan.name: Altit fort
gilgit-baltistan.description: An ancient fort at Altit town in the Hunza valley in Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan, it was originally home to the hereditary rulers of the Hunza state.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Skardu
gilgit-baltistan.description: touristâs paradise offering lush, level meadows in the form of the Deosai Plains, a dreamy lakeside resort and high-altitude desert with both sand dunes and snow.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Khunjerab
gilgit-baltistan.description: A gateway between two great allies , the incredible altitude makes for a very memorable, albeit chilly, experience, which has captured the imaginations of the local people.

gilgit-baltistan.name: K2
gilgit-baltistan.description: The legendary K2 is the second highest mountain in the world. It is located in the north-western Karakoram Mountain Range on the PakistanâChina border

gilgit-baltistan.name: Passu Cones
gilgit-baltistan.description: Breathtaking views of majestic Passu Cones (few pointed cone-like snow covered peaks) are in the Karakorum Range in north of the Gulmit village in Gojal Valley.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Rakaposhi
gilgit-baltistan.description: Part of the Karakoram range, Rakaposhi is the 27th highest mountain in the world. The mountain resides in the middle of the Bagrote valley, danyor and Nagar Valley.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Shandur Lake
gilgit-baltistan.description: Shandur Lake is located on a high mountain pass, âShandur Passâ. It is also called the âRoof of the Worldâ and is one of the most beautiful lakes of Pakistan. The spot is most well known in view of the Shandur Polo Festival.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Shandur Pass
gilgit-baltistan.description: Known as the 'Roof of the World' where the Hindu Kush, Pamir Mountains and Karakorum Range meet, Shandur is located in the Upper Chitral District of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan and is location of annual Shandur Polo Festival.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Karimabad
gilgit-baltistan.description: Karimabad, previously known as Baltit, is named after Prince Karim Aga Khan IV. It is the capital of Hunza District, in the Gilgit-Baltistan area of Pakistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Masherbrum
gilgit-baltistan.description: Masherbrum, formerly known as K1 is located in the Ghanche District, Gilgit Baltistan. At 25,659 feet, it is the 22nd highest mountain in the world.  The mighty Masherbrum Peaks in Pakistan are perfect for every tough mountaineer to prepare themselves for higher altitude peaks.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Khunjerab National Park
gilgit-baltistan.description: Khunjerab National Park is Pakistan's third largest national park. The park is adjacent to the Taxkorgan Natural Reserve in China. The primary purpose of setting up this park was to provide protection to the endangered Marco polo sheep, which is only found in this area in Pakistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Khaplu Valley
gilgit-baltistan.description: Khaplu is a city that serves as the managerial capital of the Ghanche District of Gilgit-Baltistan, in northern Pakistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Karambar Lake
gilgit-baltistan.description: Karambar Lake, renowned as Qurumbar Lake, is a high height lake situated in the Ishkoman Valley bilanz in Ghizer District, Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Naltar Valley
gilgit-baltistan.description: renowned for its lakes whose waters change colours depending on the time of day. The three lakes are known by several names. According to locals, one of the lakes is called the Pari Lake because of its enchanting, deep blue colour.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Phander Valley
gilgit-baltistan.description: Phander is the name of a settlement and valley in the Gupis-Yasin District of Pakistan's reliant region of Gilgit-Baltistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Khaplu Palace
gilgit-baltistan.description: Khaplu Palace is also known as Yabgo Khar (meaning "The fort of Doqsa"), is an old fort located in Khaplu, within the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Manthal Buddha Rock
gilgit-baltistan.description: Manthal Buddha Rock refers to a giant granite rock on which an image of Buddha has incised that in all probability dates back to the eighth century.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Karakoram Mountains
gilgit-baltistan.description: The Karakoram is a mountain range spanning the borders of China, India, and Pakistan. The mountain range is a great challenge for the mountaineers & climbers the world over.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Kharpocho Skardu Fort
gilgit-baltistan.description: The Skardu fort also known as called kharapocho is a stunning and historically significant fort of the Baltistan area.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Hushe Valley
gilgit-baltistan.description: Hushe Valley is a valley in Ghanche District, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Created by the Hushe River, the valley runs from Masherbrum Mountain (at 7,821 meters) and close by glaciers south to the Shyok River, inverse Khaplu.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Baha Lake
gilgit-baltistan.description: Baha Lake is also known as Khukush Langar Lake is a colossal lake lying at the feet of transcending mountains.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Katpana Desert
gilgit-baltistan.description: Katpana desert is one of its kind. Being one of the highest deserts, its temperature varies from 27 Â°C in summers to snow covered sand in winters.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Eagle Nest View point
gilgit-baltistan.description: Enjoy the best views of Hunza, away from the hustle and bustle of the main valley

gilgit-baltistan.name: Ishkoman
gilgit-baltistan.description: The Ishkoman valley lies in the north of Ghizer District in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, lining Afghanistan and the Pamir Wakhan Corridor.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Bagrote
gilgit-baltistan.description: Bagrote Valley is a valley in the Karakoram Mountain range in the GilgitâBaltistan district of northern Pakistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Nagar
gilgit-baltistan.description: In an eponymous valley with splendid scenery, Nagar is a small town. A visit during the right season, you can see trees of many different colors with lakes, rivers, and clear skies abound.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Diran peak
gilgit-baltistan.description: Standing at the height of 7,266 Meters, Diran is a sight to behold. This pyramid shaped mountain is known as the most dangerous mountain of Pakistan due to large snow caps.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Zharba Tso/Blind lake
gilgit-baltistan.description: Zharba Tso or Blind lake is a Panoramic Lake close to Shigar around 170 km away from Skardu in Pakistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Hunza Valley
gilgit-baltistan.description: Hunza is a mountainous valley in the northern part of the Gilgit-Baltistan formed by the Hunza River, bordering Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor to the north and the Xinjiang region of China to the northeast.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Amburiq Mosque
gilgit-baltistan.description: Located in Shigar, The Amburiq Mosque is one of the oldest mosques in the region.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Gilgit Chinese memorial cemetery
gilgit-baltistan.description: The Gilgit Chinese Memorial Cemetery locally known as the China Memorial is a graveyard located in Danyor, GilgitâBaltistan, about ten kilometres away from the capital city of Gilgit across the Gilgit River.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Fairy Meadows
gilgit-baltistan.description: Named by some German climbers and locally known as Jaugth, Fairy Meadows is a grassland near one of Nanga Parbat's base campsites.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Khalti Lake
gilgit-baltistan.description: Khalti Lake is located at Gupis-Yasin District, the westernmost piece of the GilgitâBaltistan locale and northernmost domain of Pakistan.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Rush Lake
gilgit-baltistan.description: Rush Lake is a high-altitude lake situated in Nagar Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan close to Rush Pari Peak. At 4,694 meters (15,400 ft), Rush is one of the most elevated high lakes on the planet.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Shigar Fort
gilgit-baltistan.description: The Shigar Fort means that The Fort on Rock. It is an old building of Baltistan set within the city of Shigar.

gilgit-baltistan.name: gilgit baltistan
gilgit-baltistan.description: Explore the untamed and stunning nature that surrounds Gilgit â from serene meadows, to calming rivers, to imposing mountains and more..

sindh.name: Bhodesar Mosque
sindh.description: This mosque with white pillars in Bhodesar is a small marble and limestone structure near the pond embankment is built in 1436 AD. It was built by Mehmood Shah Bin Zaffar Shah, ruler of Gujrat. The mosque is located 5 Km from town Nagarparkar.

sindh.name: Jain Temple
sindh.description: The temple is made of stone and consists of an open group of pillars with carved capitals. From this temple was found a beautifully carved block of marble which is now on display in the National Museum of Pakistan, Karachi.

sindh.name: Shrine of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai
Sadh Belo
sindh.description: An island on Indus River very close to the city of Sukkur, There is a Hindu temple on the island which was founded in 1823 by Swami Bakhandi Maharaj Udasi. Provides the tourist with a pleasurable experience and scenic view of River Indus.

sindh.name: Aror
sindh.description: Aror once served as the capital of Sindh. It is mentioned as an important trading center in early Buddhist literature. A massive earthquake that changed the course of the Indus River and ruined the town's mud brick building, thereby setting into play the city's decline.

sindh.name: NagarParkar
sindh.description: Nagarparkar, near the PakistanâIndia border, lies at the foot of the Karoonjhar Hills and is known for its desert scenery, granite outcrops, and rich cultural heritage. Home to ancient Jain temples, Hindu shrines, and the historic Bhodesar Mosque, it offers a unique blend of history, spirituality, and Thari cultureâespecially vibrant during the monsoon season.

sindh.name: Dreamworld Resort
sindh.description: At Dreamworld Resort, you along with your family will be able to keep yourself entertained throughout the stay. Providing a serene and tranquil gateway of quality living for the whole family and to rejuvenate ones mind and body.

sindh.name: hyderabad
sindh.description: Hyderabad, the Lion's City, with its historical architecture, rich history, and scrumptious Sindhi cuisine is one of the best go-to cities in Sindh.

sindh.name: Mubarak Village Beach
sindh.description: The crystal clear greenish-blue waters and unspoiled coastline have made this spot gain immense popularity in recent years. One can indulge in all sorts of water sports on the trip to Mubarak Village, including boating, beaching, snorkeling, and scuba diving.

sindh.name: Mirza Jani Baig Tarkhan's Tomb
sindh.description: The mausoleum of Mirza Jani Baig Tarkhan presents a picturesque and colourful sight. The brick masonry, in alternate courses of glazed dark-blue and unglazed red bricks, represents a high standard of Sindhi craftsmanship.

sindh.name: National Museum of Pakistan
sindh.description: The National Museum of Pakistan established in Frere Hall on 17 April 1950. In 1950 with a primary duty to counsel the Museum on the issues of enriching its collection through new acquisitions and purchase of antiquities and works of Arts. The Museum was shifted in Burns Garden in 1970.

sindh.name: Naukot Fort
sindh.description: The fort was used by Talpur Mirs as a strong hold cum-residence. Most probably these buildings were used as residences and a few of them for imprisoning the prisoners.

sindh.name: sindh
sindh.description: Sindh, the third largest province of Pakistan by area. Sindh's landscape consists mostly of alluvial plains flanking the Indus River, the Thar desert in the eastern portion of the province closest to the border with India, and the Kirthar Mountains in the western part of Sindh.

sindh.name: Sukkur Barrage
sindh.description: Sukkur, a historic city on the Indus River, is known for its rich heritage, iconic bridges, and the Sukkur Barrageâone of the worldâs largest irrigation systems. With landmarks like Sadhu Bela Temple, Masoom Shah Minaret, and lively bazaars, it offers a vibrant glimpse into Sindhi culture and serves as a gateway to nearby historic sites.

sindh.name: Kai Valley
sindh.description: Kai Valley presents a picturesque panorama on both sides of the road. Kai Valley is one of the rare solitary landscapes which sees the majority of tourists. It gives the impression as if the hills were once underneath sea.

sindh.name: Khaliq Dina Hall
sindh.description: Khaliq Dina Hall is a library and hall located in Karachi, Pakistan built in 1906. Currently used for various events, a library, and a room that serves as the office of a local NGO.

sindh.name: Chaukhandi tombs
sindh.description: Chaukhandi Tombs, located about 29 km east of Karachi, Pakistan, are an ancient graveyard dating back to the 15thâ18th centuries. Known for their intricate sandstone carvings and pyramid-like structures, the tombs mostly belong to the Jokhio tribe and other local clans. Carvings on the graves reflect local art, culture, and traditionsâdepicting warriors, jewelry, and symbols of honor. Blending Islamic and Hindu design, these historic tombs offer a unique glimpse into Sindhâs rich heritage. Now protected and listed on UNESCOâs Tentative World Heritage List, the site is open to visitors seeking history and quiet reflection.

sindh.name: Makli Necropolis
sindh.description: Makli Necropolis near Thatta is one of the worldâs largest graveyards, home to stunning tombs and mausoleums from the 14th to 18th century. Its rich history and intricate art make it a remarkable heritage site.

sindh.name: Mohenjo-daro
sindh.description: Mohenjo-daro, built around 2500 BCE near Larkana, Sindh, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a marvel of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization. Its planned streets and smart drainage reflect a highly advanced urban life.

sindh.name: Bhit Khori
sindh.description: Bhit Khori, one of the finest beaches in Pakistan, asks you to complete a rocky journey before it gifts you with its golden sands and beautiful, cerulean seawater.

sindh.name: Do Darya
sindh.description: With a great atmosphere, multiple cuisine options, and beautiful views, restaurants at Do Darya have quickly garnered a reputation and a loyal customers from all over the city. Nothing can top the experience of the Do Darya food scene.

sindh.name: Manora Beach
sindh.description: The long sandy beaches along the southern edge of the Manora Island are popular as Manora beach that is serving tourists as a popular picnic spot due to its incredible geographical location.

sindh.name: Keenjhar Lake Resort
sindh.description: The resort is developed on the bank of Keenjhar lake, which is a favorable and ideal place for winter migratory birds that come from regions of North Asia in the winter season. Located in the center of Thatta district, which has important tourist sites belonging to the near and far past of history.

sindh.name: Empress Market
sindh.description: Built at the time of Queen Victoria, Empress market considered as the most populous and crowded area of the city. Mass number from all of Karachi come to this place for shopping.

sindh.name: Old Jamia Masjid Thatta
sindh.description: The large brick masonry structure, built by Samma ruler Jam Tamachi, as homage to the Sufi saint. The masonry walls are in a highly degraded state with a collapsed roof showing its age.

sindh.name: Karachi: The City of lights
sindh.description: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan. With its dazzling bazaars, high-end shopping malls, amazing sightseeing options, and a mix of all cultures, it is surely a must-visit.

sindh.name: Gorakh Hill
sindh.description: Gorakh Hill is a hill station of Sindh.  It is situated on one of the highest plateaus of Sindh, spread over 2,500 acres. The hill station is well known for itâs nightlife, especially for itâs bonfires.

sindh.name: Meeran Ja Qubba
sindh.description: The tombs of Talpur Mirs have been built since the British conquest. From an architectural point of view they are conspicuously inferior to those of Kalhoras. For some time these tombs were maintained by their families.

sindh.name: Lansdowne Bridge
sindh.description: The Lansdowne Bridge is a 19th-century bridge that spans the Indus River between the cities of Sukkur and Rohri, in Sindh.

sindh.name: Faiz Mahal
sindh.description: A grand architectural masterpiece, unique traditional culture and traditional work of art seems to have swept over the real splendor. Details on the walls of the palace are exquisitely designed, exhibiting the fine art of the people of past era.

sindh.name: Mohatta Palace Museum
sindh.description: The Mohatta Palace Museum offers a diverse range of activities for both the casual and informed visitor. Families and school children are particularly welcome and tours can be arranged in advance.

sindh.name: Kotdiji Fort
sindh.description: This magnificent fort made from kiln baked bricks sits atop a high semi-circular lime stone hillock. Fifty strategically erected bastions for cannons and to keep a vigilant eye over enemy movement. Its beautifully carved arches & the platform attract the visitors eye immediately.

sindh.name: Umerkot Fort
sindh.description: The walls both on its interior & exterior give a tapered look, well supported on all the four corners with semi-circular bastions. On the east side there is an arched gateway flanked by semi-circular bastions.

sindh.name: Haram of Talpur Mirs
sindh.description: Mir Haram is another simple but impressive building situated inside the Pucca Fort, The interior of the Haram is profusely decorated with fresco paintings, though of degenerated quality.

sindh.name: Mirs Tombs, Khairpur
sindh.description: Khairpur, in northern Sindh, was once the capital of the Talpur princely state. Known for its royal heritage, Faiz Mahal, historic forts, Sufi shrines, handicrafts, and lush date orchards, it offers a rich blend of history, culture, and rural charm for heritage and spiritual tourism.

sindh.name: Gori Temple
sindh.description: Despite the effects of fire and gun powder, it is the best surviving temple here, built of local stone with pillars and details of marble from Rajputana.  The shrine itself which formerly had a âSikharaâ of typical Kathiawar type is now adorned with rows of miniature âSikharasâ.

sindh.name: Buddhist Stupa Nawabshah
sindh.description: A solid cylindrical structure, tapering at the top, constructed with a brick casing about 60 feet in height stands over a square base about 66 feet in each side. Located in the village of Thul Mir Rukan.

sindh.name: Sindhi Muslim Food St
sindh.description: A popular spot for all the foodies out there, from BBQ to mouth watering burgers. This food street will make anyone want to visit it over and over again.
